paragraphs.notes: Continuation of the Markush substituent-class list that runs across these pages; the page opens and closes mid-list, carries no printed paragraph marker, and the marker above is descriptive, not printed. Which symbol (R1, R2 and so on) this list defines is not determinable from this page alone, so it is not stated here. The terms are German chemical class names, so zh and en differ: German 'Alkinyl' is rendered 'alkynyl' and the German capitalisation of nouns is dropped in English. Three words are broken by the line end and are rejoined here without an added space, the printed hyphen being part of the word: 'Dialkylsulfonyl-N-' plus 'alkyl-amino', 'Cycloalkenyl-alkinylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-' plus 'amino', and 'Heterocyclyl-alkinylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-' plus 'amino'. 'cycloalkenylalkenylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' is printed with a lowercase initial c, alone among its neighbours; kept as printed. Hyphenation inside the terms is inconsistent as printed and is not normalised: 'Cycloalkyl-alkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' against 'Cycloalkylalkenylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino', and 'Heteroaryl-sulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' against 'Heteroarylsulfonylamino' on the opening lines. Two apparent gaps in the enumeration are transcribed as printed and are not corrected: 'Heterocyclylalkyl, Heterocyclylalkenyl, Heterocyclylalkinyl' break the surrounding run of '...carbonyl' terms and are printed with no carbonyl ending; and the '...carbonyloxy' run goes straight from 'Cycloalkylcarbonyloxy' to 'Cycloalkylalkenylcarbonyloxy' with no 'Cycloalkylalkylcarbonyloxy' between them. The list ends on a comma at the foot of the page and continues on the next page. A small stray ink mark sits above 'alkyl-amino' in 'Alkinylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' on the fourth line, and a faint dot sits in the left margin just before 'WO' in the header; both are scan dirt, not characters.
